items.title: Palworld dev says the studio still calls itself indie because of its "genuine creative freedom"
items.content:
Pocketpair’s John Buckley contemplates what makes a studio indie, asserting that the most important factor is its level of creative control.

Palworld might have reached a whopping 40 million players this year, but developer Pocketpair still thinks of itself as an indie studio. It's a term that's become increasingly difficult to parse in recent years, gradually growing less and less defined. Does a small developer backed by a major publisher, like Expedition 33's Sandfall Interactive, count? What about a small subsidiary of a bigger company, such as Dave the Diver's Mintrocket? Or in Pocketpair's case, a team that has rapidly grown thanks to the sheer success of its companion-collecting survival game ?

"Where does the indie line begin and end?" Head of Publishing and Communications John 'Bucky' Buckley ponders the question in response to a contemplative piece on the topic from Japanese gaming outlet Damonge . That article bounced off comments made by Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe in an interview with VGC that it's "a true indie company" and intends to "keep making games in that indie way," despite admitting that the studio's size and success could be considered "approaching the double-A level."

Speaking via X, Buckley writes, "We consider ourselves indie because we have zero outside investment or backing. Palworld and Pocketpair are entirely self-funded, but it's understandable that our success makes people see us differently." He points out that "many studios considered 'indie,' including some that have won major awards and achieved huge success, have received funding and backing from much larger companies."

He concludes that while it's tempting to set a specific employee headcount at which the indie label no longer applies, it's not a clear enough definition. Instead, he argues that the term should be more about actual independence. "If a studio has genuine creative freedom, then I think it's fair to consider them independent. If another entity is exerting creative pressure or making decisions for a studio, then I think that independence becomes questionable."

This naturally includes some of those studios who are receiving external funding, as such assistance doesn't necessarily come with any loss of creative control. "I don't think having a publisher or investor automatically makes a studio any less indie," Buckley asserts .

"I know many people will disagree, and some will point to our size or the amount of money Palworld has made as reasons why we shouldn't use that label. But from our point of view, we're 100% self-owned, we have no outside investors to answer to, and we have complete freedom to make the games we want to make. That's what being indie means to us."

Defining such genres and markers has always been more about feel, and 'indie' is a particularly difficult one to wrangle. Should it be about the studio's level of control over what it's making, or does it represent the struggle that a small team with little funding must overcome to find an audience? At this point, Pocketpair has grown its own publishing arm and is working to help other indie games along that journey, including the likes of Windrose, Truckful, and Clicky Islands.

"If you'd rather call us triple-i or double-A, that's fine too," Buckley concludes. "Ultimately it's just a label and all that really matters is we're still making fun games."

items.title: Palworld Nintendo Switch 2 Port Is Possible, but Pocketpair Has No Plans Confirmed
Palworld CEO wants to bring the game to Switch 2 despite ongoing Nintendo lawsuit
Palworld developer “of course” wants the game on Switch 2 as its simply “a really amazing platform”
items.summary: Is Palworld coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Well, not yet, but developer PocketPair would like it to eventually.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Palworld developer “of course” wants the game on Switch 2 as its simply “a really amazing platform” Published:

PocketPair, the studio behind Palworld , would really like to bring its open-world monster-catching survival game Palworld to the Nintendo Switch 2 .

Still working on additional support for the game , alongside a new, in-development Animal Crossing-esque spin-off, PocketPair has brought Palworld to every console platform other than Nintendo.

While the original Nintendo Switch was a little too weak for the game, Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe explained in a discussion with VGC that a Switch 2 port makes sense. “Of course,” the developer responded when asked if they want to bring the game to the new handheld.

“First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry. It’s been an incredible platform,” he continued.

Mizobe then stressed that there needs to be the “opportunity” to bring the game to Nintendo Switch 2, which likely means sorting out the studio’s ongoing lawsuit with Nintendo. While not mentioning the lawsuit, Pocketpair personally ported Palworld to Xbox One, PS4, Xbox Series, and PS5, so there’s certainly no lack of internal opportunity.

“If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations,” Mizobe told the outlet.

PocketPair and Nintendo’s ongoing legal case over Pokemon-like game mechanics is still active, and it’s not known what will happen if PocketPair loses. However, for now, Palworld remains one of the most popular games on Steam and other consoles, and it would be a great fit on Nintendo Switch 2.

For now, PocketPair is preparing to release Palworld Version 1.1, a sizeable but not “massive” update that will continue to expand the open-world survival game. The update is currently scheduled to launch sometime in Winter 2026.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

items.title: Palworld studio still hopes to release the game on Switch 2 one day, despite being in a legal battle with Nintendo
items.summary: The developer of viral hit Palworld still wants to bring the game to Switch 2, despite ongoing legal battle with Nintendo.
items.content:
Image credit: Pocketpair News by Sherif Saed Senior Contributor Published on Oct. 28, 2026, 2:03 p.m. 1 comment Follow Palworld Prioritise us on Google Palworld , the survival crafting game featuring adorable animals seemingly inspired by Pokémon, has been embroiled in a legal battle with Nintendo over what the company alleges is patent infringement . But although the lawsuit is ongoing, Palworld developer Pocketpair still says it's keen to bring the game to Switch 2 .

Speaking to VGC , Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he "of course" wants to bring the game to Nintendo's console. "First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry. It's been an incredible platform.

"If there's ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we'd love to have those conversations."

This stance isn't particularly surprising; Mizobe previously said it would be difficult to bring Palworld to the original Switch given how demanding the game is, but that could change if Switch 2 - the specs of which had yet to be revealed - has hardware capable enough to run the game. One year later, Pocketpair communications director John Buckley told IGN that a Switch 2 port was worth considering, assuming the console could handle the game.

Still, technical capabilities aside, we're not likely to see Palworld on Switch 2 until the lawsuit between Pocketpair and Nintendo is resolved. We're scheduled to hear an update on it soon, as the Tokyo District Court is set to issue a preliminary view on 9th November.

Palworld has sold over 30 million copies since its release in 2024, with July's 1.0 update attracting almost 1 million concurrent players on Steam .

items.title: Pocketpair would ‘love to have conversations’ to bring Palworld to Switch 2, CEO says
items.summary: Nintendo’s lawsuit surrounding the game is ongoing, but Pocketpair would like to bring Palworld to Switch 2…
items.content:
Nintendo’s lawsuit surrounding the game is ongoing, but Pocketpair would like to bring Palworld to Switch 2

Video Game News 27th Oct 2026 / 6:07 pm Posted by Chris Scullion The CEO of Pocketpair says he would love to see Palworld come to Nintendo Switch 2 in the future.

Back in June 2024, before the game’s release, Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he thought a Switch port would be unlikely due to the console’s technical capabilities.

This was seconded in an IGN interview with Pocketpair communications director John Buckley in March 2025, who said Palworld [113 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/palworld/ >Palworld is “a beefy game” that wouldn’t be possible on Nintendo Switch [6,287 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/switch/ >Switch , but that a Nintendo Switch 2 [1,639 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/nintendo-switch-2/ >Switch 2 port was “100% worth considering” if the specs (which weren’t known yet) were powerful enough.

Now, in a new interview with VGC , Mizobe was asked whether a Switch 2 port of Palworld was being considered as a real possibility, now that the specs are known to be capable enough to handle many of the current-gen games seen on other platforms.

“Of course,” Mizobe told us. “First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry. It’s been an incredible platform.

“If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations.”

Pokemon and Nintendo filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Pocketpair over two years ago now, but even last year, prior to the Switch 2's launch, Pocketpair communications lead and publishing manager John "Bucky" Buckley said that porting Palworld to the platform was "100% worth considering" as long as the console was "beefy enough" to handle it.

He's clearly not just saying that, either. After all, Pocketpair launched another of its games, the roguelike tower defense and card game title Overdungeon, on Switch at the start of last year, so the lawsuit isn't making it avoid Nintendo's platforms entirely.

Perhaps when the lawsuit has been resolved – one way or another – we could finally see Palworld on the platform. After all, it's certainly "beefy" enough to support the likes of Cyberpunk 2077, the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy, and Elden Ring.

items.title: Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld’s success
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio won’t let Palworld’s success dictate what comes next…
items.content:
Interview Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld’s success Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio won’t let Palworld’s success dictate what comes next

There’s an openness to Palworld developer Pocketpair that feels unusual in the games industry.

Its office in Gotanda, an up-and-coming entertainment district in Tokyo, is almost entirely open plan. From the CEO’s desk to the kitchen vending machines, there are no dividing walls, and the developer seems unconcerned with maintaining the air of secrecy that surrounds so many Japanese studios – even with a news journalist strolling around.

On social media, it has one of the most active community managers in the business, and visitors are often welcomed to drop by, stroll through its banks of developer desks, and have a go on the Palworld [113 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/palworld/ >Palworld -branded UFO catcher. It’s a far cry from other famous Japanese studios, which have been known to limit visits to closed meeting rooms and, sometimes, deny requests to use the bathroom.

Its approachability is particularly striking for a developer whose breakout success brought it a level of scrutiny that few independent studios experience. Palworld was barely out of the gate when its creature designs and eclectic combination of familiar mechanics attracted accusations of being derivative.

And then, of course, there was the Japanese lawsuit brought by The Pokémon Company , which alleges patent infringement, separate from the criticism that some of its creature designs bear conspicuous similarities to existing Pokémon video games [1,333 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/pokemon/ >Pokémon (with some later redesigned ).

At VGC, we extensively covered the controversy around Palworld in its early days and, more recently, published a 3/5 review of its 1.0 update . In my experience, other studios might have hunkered down, but it’s admirable that none of this changed Pocketpair’s willingness to talk.

Rather than dismissing our coverage, Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe [76 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/people/takuro-mizobe/ >Takuro Mizobe was keen to hear my take on why Palworld, a game that has clearly resonated hugely with players, so far has a critical consensus that doesn’t quite match the enthusiasm of players. The only off-limits topic was that Nintendo [6,917 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/ >Nintendo lawsuit, which Pocketpair said they couldn’t legally comment on.

Mizobe attributes Pocketpair’s openness to its unusual origins. Founded in 2015, the company grew out of his experience in web and technology businesses, rather than the traditional Japanese games industry.

“When I think about it, perhaps the Japanese games industry is a little more closed,” he told VGC. “But I don’t think that’s because companies are trying to hide anything or because they don’t want to be transparent.

“Historically, Japanese companies have placed a lot of importance on protecting their employees, maintaining security, and protecting information. Without going too deeply into the history of Japanese business, there have been a lot of hard lessons learned over the years.

“But Pocketpair didn’t really start in that traditional way. We started as a group of friends coming from web culture, and we’ve always had a very open-source kind of culture. Very early on, we set up a Discord server for our players, and we’ve always had this very open style of communication with our community.”

That culture has survived a transformation few could have predicted when Mizobe formed the company in 2015 with fellow university students. Pocketpair’s first game, card-action title Overdungeon, established its formula of combining eclectic genres together. Its next game, the Zelda- and Minecraft [376 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/minecraft/ >Minecraft -inspired Craftopia, gave Pocketpair its first big hit, selling over one million copies.

But nothing could prepare it for the near-overnight success of Palworld’s early access version, which launched for Xbox [11,896 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/xbox/ >Xbox and PC [13,156 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/pc/ >PC in January 2024 and amassed 25 million players in a single month (it now has more than 40m, according to the studio).

items.title: Pocketpair Indie Spirit: 100% Not in Palworld [2026]
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio keeps its indie spirit and won't put 100% of resources into Palworld. What is confirmed and what is not.
items.content:
Video Games Chronicle reports that Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe wants the Palworld studio to keep its indie spirit, even as the company grows big enough to look like something else from the outside. The headline is a refusal: Pocketpair will not put 100% of its resources into Palworld. Mizobe said the game will continue, just in different ways, and that the team still wants room for new and sometimes smaller projects.

What Takuro Mizobe Actually Said About Palworld’s Future Why Pocketpair Won’t Put 100% of Its Resources Into Palworld What “different ways” can mean for a live game The Pocketpair Indie Spirit Claim: Independence Is About Governance The AA Admission: Where Size Meets Freedom Small Projects and the Publishing Arm Verified Quotes From the Interview What Is Confirmed and What Is Not How Outlets Covered the Story Palworld on Switch 2 and the Legal Backdrop Historical Context: What Happens to Studios After a Breakout Competitive Comparison: Three Paths After a Breakout Hit Market Impact for Players, Rivals and Investors Five Predictions for Pocketpair What to Watch Next FAQ Who is Takuro Mizobe? Will Pocketpair keep supporting Palworld? Does Pocketpair still call itself indie? Is Pocketpair putting all its resources into Palworld? Is Palworld coming to Nintendo Switch 2? What is Pocketpair’s publishing business for? How big is Pocketpair now? Has Pocketpair announced its next game? Related Coverage The interview ran on October 27, 2026, and VGC updated its coverage on October 28. IGN, TechPowerUp and My Nintendo News followed with their own takes, most of them focused on Mizobe’s separate remarks about Palworld and Nintendo Switch 2 . The timing is hard to miss, because Nintendo’s own indie showcase lands the same day, as we covered in our Nintendo Indie World showcase preview . The question of what “indie” still means after a mega-hit has rarely felt more current.

This piece sticks to what the sources confirm. In the material we reviewed, Pocketpair has not disclosed a current headcount, revenue figure, budget, next game title, platform, price or release window. We do not guess at any of them. What we can do is read the stated strategy closely, compare it with the paths other studios take after a breakout, and lay out what to watch next.

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

Strip away the headlines and the interview makes five distinct points. First, Palworld continues. Mizobe put it plainly: “Palworld will, of course, continue, and it will continue in different ways.” Second, Pocketpair will not commit 100% of its resources to the game. Third, the company wants “to take on new challenges,” and Mizobe said some of those may be relatively small. Fourth, the company’s publishing business exists partly to help independent developers who face the kind of problems Pocketpair once faced. Fifth, Mizobe still regards Pocketpair as an indie studio.

Each point carries weight on its own. Together they describe a studio trying to hold two identities at once: the owner of a franchise that now demands long-term care, and a small-team culture that built the franchise in the first place. Mizobe does not frame these as opposites. He frames them as a balance he intends to manage, which is a more modest claim than “we will stay small forever” and a more believable one.

Igromania, the Russian games outlet, led its own report with the resource point, headlining that the Palworld creators will not put all their resources into one game. That emphasis makes sense. For readers and investors, the pledge to diversify is the most concrete signal in the whole interview, because it implies staffing and budget decisions rather than mood.

A studio with one smash hit faces a standard trap. The hit funds everything, so everything drifts toward the hit. Teams reassign to it, roadmaps bend around it, and new ideas die in planning meetings because the franchise always has a more urgent need. Mizobe’s statement reads like a deliberate attempt to avoid that drift.

The business logic is not hard to see. A single-title company carries concentrated risk. If player interest cools, if a platform changes terms, or if a legal dispute drags on, the whole firm feels it at once. Spreading effort across several projects, including small ones, lowers that exposure. Mizobe did not frame it in those terms, and VGC’s excerpt does not give numbers, so treat this as our reading of the incentives rather than a quoted rationale.

The phrase “it will continue in different ways” is deliberately open. It could point to a smaller dedicated team, to new platforms, to spin-off formats, or to a changed cadence of updates. The sources we reviewed confirm none of those specifics. What the phrase does rule out is a simple “all hands on deck forever” posture. Players who want constant large updates should read it with some caution, while players who worried the studio would abandon the game can take it as a continuation pledge.

Research summaries of the interview add that Mizobe prefers to think about the best way to keep Palworld going for players rather than defining it narrowly as a live-service product. That framing, if it holds, would give the team flexibility, though VGC’s available excerpt does not spell out what the alternative looks like.

Most arguments about “indie” fixate on team size or budget. Mizobe’s definition sits somewhere else. He ties the label to who holds power over decisions. In his telling, Pocketpair acts the way it wants because it does not face the same level of oversight as some other companies. That is a statement about governance, not headcount.

items.title: Palworld's First Official Toy Collection Is Here, Complete With Mystery Eggs and Adorable Pals
items.summary: Collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs.
items.content:
It's a good time to be a Palworld obsessive. The game recently teased its next update, Palworld: Side by Side , coming this winter, and now collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs. It's available now on Amazon .

Decorate your desk with the frankly adorable Chillet, take everyone's favorite oversized electric menace Grizzbolt out and about, and keep the perpetually vacant-looking Relaxasaurus in your pocket to remind you not to scream at your boss.

There are four different products in the collection, starting with a range of 4-inch articulated figures featuring Foxparks, Relaxasaurus, Grizzbolt, and Lifmunk. Each comes with its own Battle FX accessory, so you can make them fight without having to worry about a raid on your base.

For those who prefer their Pals a little smaller, because it's not the size of the Pal that matters but what you do with it that counts, there's also a 3-inch collector set featuring Chillet, Grizzbolt, and Relaxasaurus ( see at Amazon ).

And because apparently collecting Pals in the game wasn't enough, there are two different mystery collections to hunt down. The Cheebee Micro Blind Mystery Pal Egg 12-Pack includes a dozen 1.5-inch mystery figures, while the Blind Egg Incubator Reveal 8-Pack offers eight miniature Pals to hatch and collect.

As always, the blind-box format means there's no guarantee you'll get the Pal you're after, so happy hunting to all the completionists out there. At least these ones won't require you to craft hundreds of Pal Spheres.

The collection is available to pre-order now on Amazon .

guides, warning displays, and recommended equipment displays while fishing ・Added “Fish Behavior During Fishing Minigames” to World Settings ▼Items and Rewards ・The Echoing Flute can now be dropped from the inventory ・Changed the Pal required by the Pal Critic in Sakurajima from Selyne to Dogen ・Changed the Pal required by the Pal Critic in Sunreach from Bastigor to Faleris Aqua ▼Bases and Building ・When canceling work at production facilities, returned materials now go back to the inventory ・When canceling construction or dismantling a building, if the “Do not automatically pick up items over the weight limit” option is enabled, only returned materials exceeding the weight limit will be dropped at the player’s feet ・When building restrictions are enabled in the server settings, added areas where building is not allowed around the Field Boss Suzaku in the desert, the desert Main Mission cave, and some mission locations in Sakurajima ・Adjusted the collision of the Ancient Material Synthesizer ・Changed the specification so that players, summoned Pals, and Base Pals no longer catch fire when coming into contact with player-built Campfires ・Added a server setting for administrators to set a per-player limit on the number of buildings that can be built in the world ▼Field and Exploration ・Adjusted terrain and water display in Sunreach, the World Tree area, and other locations ・Adjusted the position and behavior of updrafts ・Adjusted the positions of NPCs, field objects, and Pal spawns ▼Sound ・Added and adjusted effects and sound effects for Oil Rig and elemental treasure chests ・Added and adjusted sound effects for item pickup, item use, crafting completion, and more ・Added and adjusted sounds for some Pals, NPCs, and field effects ▼UI and Controls ・Added name search to the Palpedia ・Added explanations for Work Suitability details to the Pal status UI and Palpedia UI ・Added passive effect and item description displays to Bounty Token acquisition notifications ・Added support for opening chat from the Radial Menu on PS5 ・Changed the default FPS cap to 120 on PC ・Version mismatch errors now show the version of the connection target ▼Performance and Stability Improvements ・Reduced load from some rendering processes, foliage display, and effect playback ・Reduced stuttering when some passive skills activate ・Reduced field rendering load in the World Tree area and other locations ▼Major Bug Fixes▼ ▼Crashes and Progression Issues ・Fixed an issue where controls could stop working after being returned to the title screen due to a connection error during loading ・Fixed an issue where a Pal could no longer be summoned again if it was recalled immediately after being summoned ・Fixed a crash that could occur when specific actions were performed while NPC dialogue and riding overlapped ・Fixed a crash that could occur during the animation after a fishing spot disappeared ・Fixed a crash that could occur when trying to display a long mission description ・Fixed a server crash that could occur when sorting Pals ・Fixed an issue where controls could stop working when switching maps while setting a custom marker on the map ▼Multiplayer and Servers ・Fixed an issue in Co-op where joining players might not correctly join the host’s guild ・Fixed an issue in Co-op where the host’s mission could progress when a client entered a mission progression area ・Fixed an issue on Dedicated Servers where the crafting display could remain on screen ・Fixed an issue where Voice Chat settings might not be applied correctly ・Fixed an issue in the Arena where the opponent’s Pal could not be targeted ▼Missions and Progression ・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Guardian would not appear later in the Main Mission if Panthalus was defeated before progressing the Main Mission ・Fixed an issue in the Main Mission “Crafting an Axe and a Pickaxe” where the objective would not progress if the player already owned or had equipped an axe or pickaxe before accepting the mission ・Fixed an issue where performing specific actions after ending dialogue with an NPC could prevent further dialogue ▼Pals and NPCs ・Fixed an issue where logging work would not occur for trees that respawned inside a base ・Fixed an issue where Visitors could spawn in unreachable locations ・Fixed an issue where dialogue would no longer occur if an NPC inside a base entered combat during dialogue ▼Partner Skills and Passive Skills ・Fixed an issue where Killamari Primo’s Partner Skill Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 effects were reversed ・Fixed an issue where Mutated Eggs increased by Grintale’s Passive Skill did not reflect mutated stat values ・Fixed an issue where the Idiosyncratic mutation passive did not activate correctly ・Fixed an issue where the defense bonus from the Lucky passive was not activating ・Fixed an issue where the Passive Skill “Mercy Hit” was not correctly applied to attacks by Pals while riding ▼Battle and Skills ・Fixed an issue where warning indicators could fail to appear during certain attacks in the World Tree boss battle ・Fixed an issue where removing a skill while it was being used could prevent that skill from being used afterward ・Fixed an issue where some attacks used by summoned Pals while other skills were on cooldown could also put unused skills on cooldown ・Fixed an issue that could occur when interrupting Ophydia’s exclusive skill “Lotus Bloom” ・Fixed an issue where Pals revived in the Arena would not continue fighting ・Fixed an issue in some Raid Boss battles where the boss could fail to temporarily stop moving after taking a certain amount of damage, or fail to summon smaller Pals correctly ・Fixed an issue where aiming while riding could make movement speed extremely slow ・Fixed an issue where wild Pals could use some skills through walls or in other situations where they could not see the player ▼Items and Shops ・Fixed an issue where selling multiple items at a shop could calculate the sale amount incorrectly ・Fixed an issue where item counts could fail to update correctly under certain conditions when moving items ・Fixed an issue where Radiant Gems dropped by wild Pals in the World Tree area could have mismatched or overly biased elements ▼Bases and Building ・Fixed an issue where color picking and editing could fail to work correctly in Paint Mode ・Fixed an issue where diagonally connecting corner roofs could result in unnatural placement ・Fixed an issue where stairs placed on the side of a corner roof could face an unnatural direction ・Fixed an issue where Worker Pal assignments might not be correctly reflected in Base Facilities ・Fixed an issue where chest access permissions were not correctly applied to material reference and consumption when crafting at a base ・Fixed an issue where the work speed multiplier would not be correctly applied after resuming the game with the Ancient Material Synthesizer ▼UI, Display, and Text ・Fixed an issue on the World Select screen where the displayed multiplayer setting could differ from the actual setting ・Fixed an issue where some key icons could appear as Xbox controller icons when using a PS5 controller on PC ・Fixed an issue where operating the chat UI with a gamepad could unintentionally close chat ・Fixed an issue where hold input did not work correctly for Pal Soul enhancement ・Fixed an issue where the HUD ammo count could remain at 0 after reloading a regular weapon ▼Field and Map ・If the map around an unlocked Watchtower remains unexplored, accessing the same Watchtower again will now unlock the map ・Fixed an issue where temperature might not be applied correctly on Bicornis Islet ・Fixed an issue where items dropped from gathering objects in the field could become buried in the ground ▼Fishing ・Fixed an issue where the fishing reward display could show the same type of item in multiple slots ▼Sound ・Fixed an issue where the Attack Chopper’s propeller sound could continue playing ・Fixed an issue where BGM could unintentionally play on the loading screen after the World Tree boss battle ・Fixed an issue where Base Raid BGM or battle BGM could unintentionally play during cutscenes ▼Mods ・Fixed an issue on Steam where Mod files could not be deleted correctly ▼Other Minor Bug Fixes▼ ・Fixed translations for guild join, leave, login, and logout notifications ・Fixed an issue where a marker could remain after completing Main Mission “Awakening” ・Fixed an issue where the mission marker was not displayed for Sub Mission “Collecting Pure Quartz” ・Fixed the marker position for No. 1 Wildlife Sanctuary in Zoe’s sub-mission ・Fixed an issue where mission NPCs could remain standing upright after death ・Fixed an issue where NPC animations could switch unnaturally during the ending ・Fixed an issue where Panthalus’s body collision did not match its appearance ・Fixed an issue where “Mercy Hit” could be displayed even when its conditions were not met ・Fixed an issue where Paladius’s Partner Skill could summon an Alpha Necromus from the player’s party at normal size ・Fixed an issue where the collision of Logging Site II could remain during building preview ・Fixed a Palbox UI misalignment that could occur when Base Pal slots were displayed in four rows ・Fixed an issue where building name text could overlap with the power icon ・Fixed the direction of the arrow indicating the front side of the Clinic ・Fixed an issue where the guild master transfer dialog text would not be displayed correctly based on the situation ・Fixed an issue where an unnecessary key guide could appear on the Pal Effigies enhancement screen ・Fixed the turning guide icon for the Wing Pack ・Fixed an issue where a black square could appear at the edge of the map filter UI ・Fixed an issue where the Field Boss icon for Prixter Lux was not displayed correctly ・Fixed an issue where unintended Pals could be caught at some fishing spots in volcanic areas ・Fixed an issue on Dedicated Servers where attacking a sleeping Galeclaw could cause it to fall through the ground ・Fixed an issue where unintended BGM would play when starting dialogue with a Black Marketeer ＝＝＝ Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.

items.content:
Pal Tamers！

The time has come to decide who stands at the top of the Palpagos Islands. Voting for the Palworld Global Popularity Poll 2026 is officially open!

With the launch of version 1.0, our roster has expanded to over 280+ Pals, and every single one of them (plus some in-game human characters) is on the ballot! Whether you’ve been attached to Lamball since day one or fell in love with a newcomer in v1.0, it's time to support your Pals!

Cast Your Vote:

https://2026.palworld-vote.com/
